findings.note: Item 1 answer states 'Whoever has legal authority to sign, such as an owner, trustee, executor, administrator, surviving spouse or several heirs acting together.' This is a list of legal roles with authority to sell, and no ledger claim supports it (the item cites no claim ids, and clm:1 to clm:7 cover only H&S 17920.3 and Civil Code 1102/1102.6). 'Surviving spouse' and 'several heirs acting together' are case-specific probate and title conclusions. The brief itself says the guide states no specific probate or trust rules. Remove the role list, or rewrite it without naming who holds authority.

Item 1 is an authority and probate answer with no confirm-with-a-professional language. Add that authority depends on who holds title and the situation, and that the seller should confirm with a real estate or probate attorney or a title company before acting.

The unit has 3 items; the unit note asks for 5-7. Items 2 and 3 (title company and what is recorded; CPA and tax) state no law, figure or promise and are acceptable, but are not drawn from the brief's fan-out questions. Editorial point only; if the writer adds items on disclosure, cleanout or code enforcement, cite the ledger claims and keep each threshold and decider (clm:2, clm:3 and clm:4 name a health officer or fire chief).
